correctness.rationale: Conjugacy/centralizer parametrization exhausts all simple modules. The accepted published indicator sum is evaluated in four cases using the invertibility of each nonidentity complement difference operator. The nonzero-kernel character sum and the complement special u=1,h0^-1 cases introduce precisely the displayed A[k] factors; all remaining roots contribute N-1 and nonroots zero. Orbit divisibility proves integrality. The maximal-dimension indicators reconstruct each |A[ell]| because complement order is coprime to |A|. The scalar/nonscalar order-147 witness is nonisomorphic by invariant conjugation type. Independent group-product enumeration over small fields and nonelementary abelian kernels agreed.

originality.rationale: The complete parameter-uniform indicator formula, torsion kernel reconstruction, and fixed-point-free-action blind multiset are not supplied by the closest examined theorems. Keilberg computes overlaps with cyclic kernel/prime-order automorphism; general Drinfeld-double identities of Kashina–Sommerhäuser–Zhu and Schauenburg require a new family-specific solution count; Iovanov–Mason–Montgomery address general integrality rather than this full distribution. Direct index and source searches revealed no stronger family classification. Residual historical-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: An older equivalent result could appear under metacyclic or group-theoretical fusion category terminology and was not conclusively excluded.

General published double-indicator formulas are logically strong computational tools; the novelty assessment is for their fully evaluated uniform family formula and the indicator-rigidity limitation, not for the universal identity itself.

value.rationale: Complete higher indicators of Drinfeld doubles are natural tensor-category invariants. The uniform formulas treat arbitrary finite abelian kernels and arbitrary fixed-point-free cyclic complements at all indices, including torsion effects absent in elementary abelian cases. The theorem proves a sharp representation-invariant reconstruction/nonreconstruction boundary: the indicators determine A and m but not the action, with explicit nonisomorphic groups of order 147. This is structural information, not just an isolated small count.
